record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: For higher-genus correlation functions of rational conformal field theories, can one prove convergence of the series built from intertwining operators, so that their sums define functions on Teichmuller spaces and yield higher-genus chiral and full correlation functions?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Prove the convergence of these series obtained using intertwining operators to construct higher-genus correlation functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a rational vertex operator algebra (satisfying the standard finiteness and reductivity conditions that make its module category a modular tensor category), and for each genus $g \geq 1$ consider the formal series built from compositions of intertwining operators among $V$-modules that are used to construct higher-genus chiral correlation functions on Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary components. These series are indexed by insertions of intermediate modules along a pants decomposition of a genus-$g$ surface and depend on local coordinates and on moduli of the surface.

Prove that for every such configuration the series converges absolutely on the appropriate domain in the (infinite-dimensional) Teichmüller space of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary, so that its sum extends to a well-defined function on Teichmüller space. Show moreover that suitable combinations of these sums yield higher-genus chiral correlation functions (multivalued analytic functions on the moduli space of Riemann surfaces with marked points and local coordinates) and that pairing chiral and antichiral blocks via a modular-invariant assignment produces single-valued higher-genus full correlation functions of the corresponding rational conformal field theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The convergence of the higher-genus series built from intertwining operators is described as a major open problem, requiring conjectures on functions over infinite-dimensional Teichmüller spaces and moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundaries. Recent progress (Radnell–Schippers–Staubach on the moduli spaces, and modular invariance results for logarithmic intertwining operators) addresses related sub-problems, but the full higher-genus convergence statement does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Prove the convergence of these series obtained using intertwining operators to construct higher-genus correlation functions.
status_evidence.claim: The higher-genus convergence is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Convergence in Conformal Field Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses convergence problems in CFT including higher-genus aspects.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence problems remain a central topic of ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Modular Invariance of (Logarithmic) Intertwining Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Proves modular invariance for pseudo-traces of products of geometrically-modified intertwining operators.
status_evidence.claim: Related modular invariance results have been obtained, but not full higher-genus convergence.
